comment: The artifact table: the manifest, the hashes and the write protocol of
src/fort/library/artifact.ft, the declarations and the external globals of
an interface module in src/fort/gen_fir.ft and src/fort/gen_data.ft, and the
library build of src/fort/driver.ft (D9.11, toolchain.md 2.1 and 2.2,
module-system.md 10.4). Each row breaks one rule that a stage holds. The
module suites compile the mutated module themselves; the build links the
compiler so that the md5 guard reads it, and the last stage runs the ctest
library-artifact over that compiler. The table runs in the VM with the
default runner after `tools/vm configure` and `tools/vm build`.
The build waits 2 s and touches the sources in the guest first. The shared
folder keeps whole seconds of mtime, so a mutation that the host wrote in
the second of the baseline output looked old to ninja, which built nothing:
the first round of each run read `stale` until this change.
D9.11-summaries-errno survives in the VM: there the AT_REMOVEDIR form of
unlinkat(2) gives EACCES for a file in a directory that the process cannot
write, as the first call does. On darwin it gives ENOTDIR, and
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/library/artifact.ft src/fort/gen_data.ft src/fort/gen_fir.ft src/fort/driver.ft && cmake --build build/Linux/debug --target fort

stages.name: the artifact module suites
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --verify-ir library/artifact gen_interface driver_artifact driver_library

stages.name: the artifact of std
stages.command: python3 test/library/artifact_test.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu --opt opt-18

mutations.what: a manifest value keeps `\` as it is
a manifest value keeps a space as it is
an escaped byte of a value has lowercase hex digits
mutations.old:
strbuf.push(out, UPPER_HEX[byte >> HEX_SHIFT]);
            strbuf.push(out, UPPER_HEX[byte & HEX_MASK]);
mutations.new:
strbuf.push(out, LOWER_HEX[byte >> HEX_SHIFT]);
            strbuf.push(out, LOWER_HEX[byte & HEX_MASK]);

mutations.what: a hash has uppercase hex digits
mutations.old:
strbuf.push(out, LOWER_HEX[byte >> HEX_SHIFT]);
        strbuf.push(out, LOWER_HEX[byte & HEX_MASK]);
mutations.new:
strbuf.push(out, UPPER_HEX[byte >> HEX_SHIFT]);
        strbuf.push(out, UPPER_HEX[byte & HEX_MASK]);

mutations.what: the source hash takes the modules in dependency order
the source hash covers the modules of an interface file
the source hash leaves out the byte count of each file
the source hash writes the opened path unescaped
the `cfg` and `use` lines keep the order of the caller
a line with an empty second value drops the space before it
the key covers the text that the buffer held before the manifest
the manifest and its key hold no `use` line
release mode writes `mode checked`
the writer keeps the manifest of an older build while it writes
the writer writes the manifest before the archive
a rename that fails leaves its temporary file
the writer makes no `summaries/` directory
a file of an older build stays in `summaries/`
a file in `summaries/` that unlink(2) refuses reports the ENOTDIR of rmdir(2)
the writer follows a `summaries` that is a symbolic link and empties its target
mutations.old: i32 fd = libc.open(c_path.ptr, libc.O_RDONLY | libc.O_DIRECTORY | libc.O_NOFOLLOW, 0);

mutations.what: the writer writes the files of the build before it empties `summaries/`
a file or a link at the temporary name stays and fails the write
mutations.old:
libc.unlink(c_temp.ptr);
    i32 fd = libc.open(c_temp.ptr, libc.O_WRONLY | libc.O_CREAT | libc.O_EXCL, mode);
mutations.new: i32 fd = libc.open(c_temp.ptr, libc.O_WRONLY | libc.O_CREAT | libc.O_EXCL, mode);

mutations.what: an interface function gets no `declare` line
an `extern fn` of an interface module gets a fort `declare` line
a declaration drops the extension attribute of a parameter
a declaration drops the result pointer of an aggregate result
a declaration names `#0` and the unit writes no such group
a constant of an interface module is a definition of the unit
mutations.old:
if (g->module != null && g->module->interface) {
        gen_external(g, s, name, ty);
mutations.new:
if (false && g->module != null && g->module->interface) {
        gen_external(g, s, name, ty);

mutations.what: a `mut` global of an interface module is an external constant
mutations.old:
if (s->kind == ast.sym_kind.s_global) {
        strbuf.append(&g->globals, " = external dso_local global ");

mutations.what: an artifact takes a target that the compiler was not built for
`--lib -S` takes the built target alone
the archive line writes no symbol index
the compile line of a library links in place of `-c`
the default artifact is `<name>.lib`
the artifact build leaves its object in the temporary directory
the manifest names the default archiver in place of `--ar`
`--ar` without `--lib` is no usage error
`--lib -c` writes `<name>.ll`
an archiver that a signal stops is reported with `status`
